units.title: Baal Cycle 1.1 IV: El proclaims the name of his son Yamm, 'beloved of El', promises a house of silver and orders him to drive Baal from his throne; El's feast
Baal Cycle 1.2 I: Baal curses Yamm; Yamm's envoys come to the assembly on Mount Ll; the gods bow their heads; 'Give up Baal!'; El makes Baal Yamm's slave; Anat and Athtart restrain Baal
Baal Cycle 1.2 III: Kothar goes to El at the source of the rivers and is told to build Yamm's palace; Athtar complains he has no house and no wife; Shapsh warns him El will overturn his throne
Baal Cycle 1.2 IV: Kothar promises Baal eternal kingship and makes the clubs Yagrush and Ayyamur; they strike Yamm's shoulder, then his skull; Yamm falls; 'Yamm is dead, Baal shall be king'

Baal Cycle 1.3 III 32 - IV 4: Anat trembles at the messengers: what enemy has risen against Baal? 'Did I not smite Yamm, beloved of El, River the great god, muzzle Tunnanu, smite the twisting serpent, Šalyaṭ of seven heads ...'

Baal Cycle 1.3 IV 5-55: the lads repeat Baal's message; Anat agrees to put war from the earth; she crosses a thousand fields to Ṣapan; Baal sends the women away and sets an ox before her; she bathes in dew; lament: Baal has no house like the gods; Anat will make El turn to her

Baal Cycle 1.3 II: Anat shuts her house and slaughters the people of the seashore and the sunrise: heads like balls, hands like locusts, knee-deep in blood; she fights tables and chairs, rejoices, washes her hands and bathes in dew of heaven and oil of earth
Baal Cycle 1.3 VI: a gift for Athirat; Baal sends Gapn and Ugar across sea, mountains and the heights of heaven to Qudšu-Amrur and on to Kothar in Memphis and Caphtor

Baal Cycle 1.4 I: Baal has no house; prepare a gift for Athirat; Kothar goes up to the bellows and pours silver and gold into a canopy, couch, throne, footstool, sandals?, a table full of all the beasts of earth's foundations and a bowl with wild bulls

Baal Cycle 1.4 II: Athirat with her spindle washes her garment in the sea; she trembles at the approach of Baal and Anat, 'have they come to slay my sons?', then sees the gleam of silver and gold and rejoices; she calls her fisherman

Baal Cycle 1.4 III: Baal complains he was mocked and spat on in the assembly of the sons of El; Baal hates three feasts: of shame, of strife and of the handmaids' lewdness; Baal and Anat give gifts to Athirat; feast

Baal Cycle 1.4 IV: Athirat rides a saddled donkey to El at the source of the rivers; El laughs and offers her food, wine or his love; 'our king is Baal'; Baal has no house; El: am I a slave, is Athirat a handmaid, to mould bricks?
Baal Cycle 1.1 V: days pass; someone seeks Haddu on Ṣapan; 'you will bind me, Bull El, among the stones' (fragment)

Baal Cycle 1.4 VI: 'you will come back to my word'; cedars from Lebanon and Sirion; fire burns in the house six days and on the seventh the silver has become plates and the gold bricks; Baal feasts his brothers, the seventy sons of Athirat

Baal Cycle 1.4 VII: Baal takes sixty-six cities; he orders the window opened, a rift in the clouds; he gives his holy voice, the earth quakes, the mountains tremble, his enemies flee to the forests; 'I alone rule the gods'; messengers to Mot

Baal Cycle 1.6 II: like a cow's heart for her calf, Anat's heart longs for Baal; she seizes Mot by the hem: 'give me my brother'; Mot: 'I put him in my mouth like a lamb'; Anat splits Mot with a blade, winnows, burns, grinds and sows him; birds eat him

Baal Cycle 1.6 V: Baal strikes the sons of Athirat and sits on his throne; in the seventh year Mot returns: 'because of you I suffered shame, winnowing, burning, grinding, sifting, scorching, sowing in the sea; give me one of your brothers to eat'
El's instructions - sacrifice on the tower, muster of the whole people, seven-day march, siege of Udum, demand for Hurriya (Kirta II-III)

KTU 1.12 I: the handmaids complain to El that 'they' devour their liver; El laughs in his heart and sends them into the wilderness to crouch and bear the Devourers and Renders, horned like bulls, with Baal's face; Baal hunts them at the edge of the steppe, burning with desire
El takes two women at the shore; they bear Shahar and Shalim and the gracious gods, who are sent to the holy desert for seven years (KTU 1.23 30-76)
